conviction_note: Q3 is already pre-released at the operating level (465.8 TBtu at a $6.79/MMBtu implied fee, against Q2's 466.4 TBtu at $6.45 that made $2.49bn of EBITDA), so the print turns on the 2026 guide. That guide assumed $12.50-13.50/MMBtu for unsold cargos, while TTF has run at EUR 80-100/MWh since mid-September and Cheniere raised its own guide about 10% on 29 Oct. A raise looks likely, but the last raise (11 Aug) was sold 7.3%, the option skew already pays for upside, and the stock trades day to day on TTF and Iran headlines. p_up is therefore 56, applied to an abs_move of 10, which comes to +1.2. The findings sum to +1.8; the two numbers differ because the scaled one carries the macro and reaction-function uncertainty.
bar: Q3 EPS consensus $0.50 on revenue of about $4.64bn, whisper $0.53 (Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-03, https://finviz.com/news/414164/venture-globals-q3-test-can-record-ebitda-hold-through-summer-after-three-guidance-raises; one estimate source only, so sizes on the quarter are capped small). The Q3 EBITDA bar of 'about $2.5bn, a repeat of Q2' is that same source's inference from the guide, not a consensus figure. The company-sourced bar is the 2026 adjusted EBITDA guide of $8.7-9.1bn, assuming $12.50-13.50/MMBtu for remaining unsold cargos with sensitivity of $180-210m per $1/MMBtu (Q2 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002007855/000200785526000063/vgincq22026earningsrelease.htm). print_vs_bar_pct is my estimate of Q3 adjusted EBITDA (about $2.6bn) against $2.5bn.
positioning_check: Short interest 45.44m shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 3.69 days to cover (Quiver Quant, https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Venture+Global+Stock+Short+Interest+Rises+to+83.81%25; its '83.81% of float' figure is not credible). Fintel/NYSE give 42.1m shares, 8.55% of float on Capital IQ's float figure, 2.70 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement (https://fintel.io/ss/us/vg). That is moderate, not crowded. Skew_25d is -14.18 vol points, so upside is paid; put/call OI is 0.70; the event-implied move is 8.11%. The stock is -7.96% over 5 days, -9.79% over 20 days and -32% from its 52-week high: -13% on 2 Nov, when Plaquemines Phase 1 reached COD and energy fell broadly (XLE -4%, NEXT -9.8%), then lower again as TTF fell 17.7% in a week on Iran diplomacy. Earnings Whispers puts bullish sentiment at 19%, down from 31.1% before the last report.

findings.finding: Q3 was pre-released on 7 Oct (8-K item 2.02): 465.8 TBtu sold, 124 cargos, implied weighted average fixed liquefaction fee $6.79/MMBtu, against Q2's 466.4 TBtu at $6.45/MMBtu, which produced $2,491m of adjusted EBITDA. Same volume at +$0.34/MMBtu is about +$160m, so roughly $2.6-2.65bn for Q3 if costs are flat, against the ~$2.5bn 'repeat of Q2' that previews anchor on. Five DES cargos (20.4 TBtu) shift into Q4 revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The operating pre-releases moved the stock little: 2026-07-08 +1.21%, 2026-10-07 -3.4% (the Galp award came out the same day), 2026-04-09 -0.15%. At the full Q2 print on 2026-08-11, EPS $0.51 beat the $0.49 consensus and the stock still fell 7.29%.
findings.why_not_priced: The volume and fee are public, but no preview I found turns them into an EBITDA number. Earnings Whispers still frames the bar as 'a repeat of Q2' and puts consensus EPS flat at $0.50 against $0.51. Had the arithmetic been priced, the EPS consensus would sit above Q2 rather than below it. Because the line is pre-released and inside the guide, this is sized near zero.
findings.independence: Q2 comparison figures: the Q2 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002007855/000200785526000063/vgincq22026earningsrelease.htm and the 2026-07-08 operating update (https://pgjonline.com/news/2026/july/venture-globals-liquefaction-fees-jump-69-on-higher-lng-prices). These are the same company's documents, so this is not independent confirmation.

findings.finding: The 2026 adjusted EBITDA guide of $8.7-9.1bn (set 11 Aug) values remaining unsold 2026 cargos at $12.50-13.50/MMBtu, with $180-210m of EBITDA per $1/MMBtu, which implies roughly 180-210 TBtu was open. Since then European TTF has hit EUR 79/MWh (9 Sep, highest since Dec 2022), EUR 86 (13 Oct) and about EUR 97-100 (28 Oct), and was still EUR 82 on 9 Nov, roughly $27-28/MMBtu against Henry Hub near $3. Cheniere, which reported on 29 Oct after VG last spoke, raised its 2026 guide to $8.75-9.25bn from $7.90-8.40bn. YTD EBITDA is about 1.4 + 2.5 + ~2.6 = ~6.5bn, so the current guide implies Q4 of 2.15-2.55bn. Q4 open cargos realised above $20 rather than $13 would add several hundred million dollars, and the guide is likely to be raised (my estimate is +$0.3-0.9bn).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide moves at full prints: 2026-03-02 (first 2026 guide of $5.2-5.8bn) +17.44%; 2026-05-12 (raised to $8.2-8.5bn) +14.2%; 2026-08-11 (raised to $8.7-9.1bn) -7.29%. Raises have been bought twice and the most recent one was sold.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock is down 10% in 20 days and 8% in 5 days while TTF sits 165% above a year ago. If the market were pricing a raise of up to $0.9bn (around 10% of the 2026 guide, the scale Cheniere just delivered), the stock would not have fallen into the print. The 2 Nov drop also suggests the market reads COD as the end of the spot windfall. The risk is that analysts already model the raise and the market discounts it, as on 11 Aug.
findings.independence: Cheniere Q3 2026 release (call 2026-10-29), guide raised $7.90-8.40bn to $8.75-9.25bn: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000003570/000000357026000040/cei20263rdqtrerex991.htm. TTF levels: https://www.xtb.com/en/market-analysis/european-ttf-gas-futures-hit-highest-level-since-2022-as-inventories-remain-low-ahead-of-winter (2026-09-09) and https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/eu-natural-gas (2026-11-09). VG's own open-cargo count and hedging are not disclosed, so the transmission from TTF to VG is a proxy.

findings.finding: Plaquemines Phase 1 (about 13.3 mtpa) declared COD on 30/31 Oct 2026. From November its output goes to long-term SPA buyers (Shell, Orlen, Sinopec, CNOOC, EDF) at contract fees that the press notes are 'substantially lower than prevailing spot', instead of commissioning cargos sold spot. That lowers the Q4 and 2027 weighted fee base. The stock fell 13% on 2 Nov.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2 Nov 2026: -13.0%, the largest one-day fall in a year, on a day energy fell broadly (XLE -4.0%, NEXT -9.8%), so not all of it is COD.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the guide assumed Q4 COD, and the stock has already fallen 13% plus another 8%. What is left is how management sizes the Q4 drop in the fee on the call, and whether COD came earlier within Q4 than the guide assumed. Neither is disclosed yet.
findings.independence: Trefis on the 2 Nov move: https://www.trefis.com/stock/vg/articles/622177/what-just-happened-to-venture-global-stock/2026-11-03. It covers the same event, so it is not independent.

findings.finding: On 7 Oct an ICC tribunal (2-1) found that VG's Calcasieu Pass unit breached its SPA with Galp by declaring COD late. Damages are capped at $170m and will be set at a hearing in 2027 or 2028. It is the second arbitration loss after BP; the Orlen decision is still pending, and the 10-Q may update reserves or disclosure.
findings.why_not_priced: The award was disclosed a month ago and the cap is known, so it is largely priced. What remains is any 10-Q disclosure on Orlen or a change in reserves.

findings.finding: As of 11 Aug, 75% of 2027 cargos were contracted, leaving about 25% open; Plaquemines Phase 2 commissioning cargos run to mid-2027. TTF is at EUR 82 with an analyst/model 12-month view of EUR 109 and EU storage under 73% against a 90% five-year average. Any 2027 commentary or forward sales at current spreads on the call would be upside to the out-year view.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: VG gave its first 2026 guide at the Q4 print (2026-03-02, +17.44%). It has not given formal 2027 guidance at a Q3 print before; the Q3 2025 print (2025-11-10) moved +6.26%.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock is pricing a normalisation of the TTF spread (down 17.7% last week) rather than out-year cash flows at current levels. This is a proxy: the company has not said it will address 2027 on this call.

findings.finding: Commercial items since the last print: a 20-year, 1 mtpa SPA with ConocoPhillips starting 2030 (2 Oct), and framework agreements with GE Vernova and Baker Hughes for up to 16 720-MW power units, up to 10 GW at its sites (15 Oct, 8-K item 1.01). These support CP2 Phase 2 and the Plaquemines expansion, which target FID in 2027, and are likely talking points on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean reaction attributable to these announcements was found.
findings.why_not_priced: Already announced, so mostly priced. The only open part is call detail on the size or timing of these projects.

outside_window.finding: BP's damages hearing in the Calcasieu Pass arbitration is set for late November 2026. BP seeks at least $3.7bn, possibly more than $6bn before interest, and a ruling would come later still.
Galp damages hearing: expected 2027-2028, capped at $170m.

Analyst preview notes or target changes dated November 2026

rejected_candidates.detail: This is the 2025 Q3 print, not 2026; the date from context is November 2025.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Cheniere's guide raise as a separate finding
rejected_candidates.detail: Merged into the guidance finding as independent corroboration of the same fact, that the spot spread is far above the guide's assumption.

rejected_candidates.detail: The same TTF series as the guidance and 2027 findings. Its level (EUR 82) is still well above the guide's assumption; the direction of the next session's TTF move cannot be forecast and sits in p_up.

baseline_tension: The positive lean agrees with the upside-paid skew (-14 vol points), so part of it is probably priced. It cuts against the 5-day and 20-day drawdown, which reads as the market marking VG to a falling TTF and the end of Phase 1 spot sales rather than to the guide arithmetic.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar sourced from one estimate source; Q3 lands inside the guide and is pre-released): the Q3 pre-release finding moves from +0.5 to +0.3.
Lesson 1 (reaction function veto: the most recent guide raise, 2026-08-11, was sold 7.3%): the guidance finding moves from +2.0 to +1.5.
Lesson 7 (sign agrees with an upside-paid skew, so partly priced): p_up moves from 57 to 56.

Last block ('a reaction history built from the wrong events is worse than none'): I rebuilt the base rate from confirmed full prints only (2025-11-10 +6.26, 2026-03-02 +17.44, 2026-05-12 +14.2, 2026-08-11 -7.29; median |move| about 10.7) and separated out the operating pre-releases. abs_move moves from 9.0 to 10.0.
Left standing: the COD, Galp, 2027 and commercial findings are unchanged. The financing lesson does not apply. There is no crowded short (about 8.5% of float, about 3 days to cover).
